lines.trans: Is the wait getting even longer?
More people crowded in than expected, so it seems organizing the line is taking extra time.
Cindy, how about just giving in to CEO Byun this once?

words.gram: bound noun + subject particle (contracted from 것이)
adjective, to be how, with wondering question ending -eulkka

lines.trans: What?
I heard from the director that the situation right now is identical to what happened back then.
They say forcing these rookie package deals right now is just CEO Byun's preview—once the main feature starts, it gets brutal.
Does he know any news about how she is doing?
He says he has no idea at all—there are only rumors.
Rumors that she went abroad or got addicted to surgery—and not a single good story among them.

words.gram: verb, to not exist (auxiliary in -l su eopda 'cannot'), with connective -go

lines.trans: So Cindy, please just apologize to CEO Byun this one time…
Go ask how many more minutes this is going to take.
Now my own anti-fans are even inviting me to their offline meetup.

words.gloss: they say let us hold / do

words.gram: noun, next, with time particle -에 (at, on)

examples.trans: I want to give, mention and right now.
How about trying to give, mention and together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 커피 시킬 때 보면 돼요, 이름 긴 거 시키는 사람들 있거든.
examples.trans: Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
This expression comes from 'long'.

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

examples.text: 생각보다 사람들이 많이 몰려서 정리하는 데 시간이 좀 걸리나 봐.
examples.trans: More people crowded in than expected, so it seems organizing the line is taking extra time.

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 몰리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (crowded in and).

examples.text: 봐 봐라, 내가 다 정리했다. 입수는 발목까지 한대.
examples.trans: Look here, I settled everything. She agreed to enter the water up to her ankles.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 정리하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (settled, sorted out).

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used as casual past (걸렸어.).

examples.text: 이제 다 됐어, 낙서 지우는 데 좀 시간이 걸렸어. 주차장 도착하면 다시 전화할게.
examples.trans: It is all finished now—scrubbing off the graffiti took a while. I will call again once I reach the parking lot.
Let us do that (it took) right away.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Top K-pop solo singer in The Producers.

examples.trans: Cindy is getting ready in the waiting room.
Cindy's new song is very popular.

meanings.note: Honorific title (대표 + -님) commonly used for the head of an entertainment agency or company.

examples.trans: The CEO is in a meeting.
Our agency boss approved it.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Written as one word (한번) when softening a suggestion or request ('why don't we...').

examples.trans: Try eating this food.
Come visit sometime when you have time.

examples.text: 신디야, 대표님한테 그냥 한번 져드리는 게 어떨까?
examples.trans: Cindy, how about just giving in to CEO Byun this once?

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 져드리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (yielding / giving in (humble)).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
The manager came.
Hello, Manager Kim.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: noun situation

examples.trans: Situation is good.
Situation is bad.

meanings.en: the old days, old times, the past

examples.trans: In the old days, this neighborhood was quiet.
Sometimes I think of the old days.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (똑같은).

examples.text: 희한하네, 어제 승찬이도 너랑 똑같은 소리를 하더라고.
examples.trans: How funny—yesterday Seung-chan said the exact same thing you just said.

examples.text: 응, 그 남자는 좀 아닌 것 같다면서! 두 남자가 똑같은 소리를 한다는 건 그 남자가 진짜 아니라는 얘기지?
examples.trans: Yeah, saying that guy sounded questionable! If two men say the exact same thing, that guy really must be no good, right?

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

examples.text: 지금 이렇게 끼워팔기 하는 건 대표님의 예고편 같은 거래. 본편 들어가면 진짜 살벌하대.
examples.trans: They say forcing these rookie package deals right now is just CEO Byun's preview—once the main feature starts, it gets brutal.
The topic of package-deal bundling came up in today's meeting.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 지금 이렇게 끼워팔기 하는 건 대표님의 예고편 같은 거래. 본편 들어가면 진짜 살벌하대.
examples.trans: They say forcing these rookie package deals right now is just CEO Byun's preview—once the main feature starts, it gets brutal.

examples.text: 근데 너 어설프게 고백은 하지 마라. 사랑에도 예고편이 필요한 거야.
examples.trans: Still, do not blurt out a clumsy confession—even love needs a preview.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 지금 이렇게 끼워팔기 하는 건 대표님의 예고편 같은 거래. 본편 들어가면 진짜 살벌하대.
examples.trans: They say forcing these rookie package deals right now is just CEO Byun's preview—once the main feature starts, it gets brutal.
The topic of main feature / broadcast came up in today's meeting.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

examples.text: 지금 이렇게 끼워팔기 하는 건 대표님의 예고편 같은 거래. 본편 들어가면 진짜 살벌하대.
examples.trans: They say forcing these rookie package deals right now is just CEO Byun's preview—once the main feature starts, it gets brutal.
The mood on set today is truly they say it gets brutal.
Did you hear about this older sister, idol?
I was busy today because of older sister, idol.
Did you hear about this news and?
I was busy today because of news and.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

전혀.gloss: (not) at all, not in the least

meanings.note: Negative polarity adverb; almost always pairs with a negative verb or adjective (모르다, 없다, 안 ~).

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.
It's not cold at all today.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.
Is that rumour true?
A strange rumour is going around the company.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.
I'm traveling overseas.
I am overseas.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

examples.text: 해외로 갔다느니 성형 중독이 됐다느니, 그중에 좋은 얘기는 하나도 없고.
examples.trans: Rumors that she went abroad or got addicted to surgery—and not a single good story among them.
The topic of cosmetic surgery came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 해외로 갔다느니 성형 중독이 됐다느니, 그중에 좋은 얘기는 하나도 없고.
examples.trans: Rumors that she went abroad or got addicted to surgery—and not a single good story among them.
The topic of addiction came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 해외로 갔다느니 성형 중독이 됐다느니, 그중에 좋은 얘기는 하나도 없고.
examples.trans: Rumors that she went abroad or got addicted to surgery—and not a single good story among them.
The topic of among them came up in today's meeting.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Native Korean numeral; shortens to 한 before a counter noun (한 개, 한 명).

examples.trans: One coffee, please.
How much is one?

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 편집 잘하면 시련을 당하는 주인공인데 까딱 잘못하면 바보로 보일 수 있다니까!
examples.trans: edited well she is a heroine enduring trials, yet one wrong cut could make her look like a total fool!
This expression comes from 'if it goes wrong'.

examples.text: 우리도 여섯 명이어야 되는데 한 명 빈 거잖아.
examples.trans: We are supposed to have six members too, and one spot is empty.

examples.text: 촬영하고 나면 다음 주 화요일쯤에는 시간 비어.
examples.trans: After filming wraps, I have free time around next Tuesday.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.text: 너희는 사람이 몇인데 그걸 아무도 못 봤냐?
examples.trans: With so many staffers on your team, how did nobody catch that?
Here the word for 'so many, yet' is key.

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?
I want to ask right now.
How about trying to ask together tomorrow?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

examples.text: 이제 하다 하다 안티들이 나보고 정모를 하자네.
examples.trans: Now my own anti-fans are even inviting me to their offline meetup.
The topic of anti-fans came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

examples.text: 이제 하다 하다 안티들이 나보고 정모를 하자네.
examples.trans: Now my own anti-fans are even inviting me to their offline meetup.
The topic of regular offline meetup came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
